subtype: Fixing something with a family member [Actor]
passage: Family diary, Sunday. Noor writing. Our ceiling fan began to wobble, so my brother-in-law came over to fix it. Preeti, my daughter, held the ladder and passed him the tools. First he switched off the fan and the main switch and stuck tape over it with a note. Preeti asked why he loosened the blades one by one. "So they balance," he said, and showed her the small gap on one. She watched his hands more than his face. When the fan ran quietly, she said, "I could do that." He smiled and said, "Next time, you can hold the screwdriver." I have never seen her stand so straight. Noor

qa.a: He switched off the fan and the main switch and stuck tape over it with a note.

qa.q: What was Preeti feeling when she said "I could do that"?
qa.a: Preeti felt capable and proud, since she had watched the work closely and the fan ran quietly.

qa.q: What made this a good way for Preeti to learn a repair skill?
qa.a: She held the ladder, watched his hands, asked why, heard the explanation and was invited to hold the screwdriver next time.

qa.q: How does Noor see Preeti after the repair?
qa.a: Noor sees a daughter standing straighter and more confident, which shows the lasting sense of capability.

grounding: Shows a teenager helping a family member fix a fan, learning by watching hands and hearing why.

subtype: Fixing something with a family member [Actor]
passage: Sunday. Rafiq chacha said the back tyre of my cycle was flat again, and instead of doing it himself he said, "Bring the bucket." First he showed me how to take the tube out. Then I filled the bucket and pushed the tube through the water. Tiny bubbles came out of one spot, and chacha put his finger on it. "See? That's your hole." He told me to rough up the rubber, and why the glue needs to dry a little before the patch. I did the patch with my own hands. It looked ugly but held air. I rode round the lane three times. Nobody had to tell me I was proud. Afreen

qa.q: What did Rafiq chacha ask Afreen to bring?
qa.a: Rafiq chacha asked Afreen to bring the bucket.

qa.q: What was Afreen feeling when riding around the lane three times?
qa.a: Afreen was proud and delighted, since the patch was ugly but held air.

qa.q: What made the learning stick for Afreen?
qa.a: Afreen did the steps with own hands while Rafiq chacha showed what to do and explained why, such as letting the glue dry a little before the patch.

qa.q: How might Rafiq chacha feel watching Afreen fit the patch?
qa.a: Rafiq chacha is probably patient and happy to pass on a skill, letting Afreen do the work instead of doing it himself.
